title: Applied ML eval harness: Onboarding, prompt sets, quantization, quality guardrails, and regression triage
author: Maya Patel
content:
Summary:
This playbook describes the end-to-end applied-ML evaluation (eval) harness process used at Redwood Inference. It consolidates guidance and runbooks for model onboarding, prompt set and benchmark management, quality guardrails, quantization profile integration, and regression triage. The goal is to ensure consistent quality, repeatable evaluations, and rapid regression detection for model deployments across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private modes.

1) Scope and audience
- Scope: evaluation and quality assurance for any model intended for production serving on the Redwood platform (text generation, chat, embeddings, reranking).
- Audience: ML Engineers, Applied ML, SRE, Product Engineers, and Solutions Engineers responsible for model onboarding, evals, and production rollouts.

2) High-level workflow (overview)
1. Request onboarding: team opens an onboarding request via the eval-harness intake template.
2. Baseline evaluations: run standard benchmark suite and resource/latency profiling.
3. Quality gating: apply guardrails (safety, hallucination, factuality, style) to determine pass/fail.
4. Quantization profiling: test candidate quantization profiles and collect accuracy vs. perf tradeoffs.
5. Regression triage: on any quality regression, run triage playbook and coordinate fixes.
6. Release authorization: product/owner signs off and model is added to model catalog with serving profile.

3) Eval harness components
- Runner: the eval harness runner executes prompt sets as reproducible jobs (k8s jobs or local Docker).
- Prompt catalog: stored as versioned YAML/JSON files with metadata (dataset id, owner, tags, expected behavior).
- Metrics store: time-series and per-prompt result store (Prometheus + ClickHouse or equivalent) for trend analysis.
- Artifacts: outputs, seed RNG, model config, quantization artifacts, and environment recorded for reproducibility.

4) Onboarding checklist (step-by-step)
- Pre-checks (owner/team):
  - Confirm model architecture and license (open or commercial).
  - Provide model artifact location (s3/GCS) and inference container or weights + conversion instructions.
  - Fill intake template: use the eval-harness intake Confluence page and link the PR.
- Baseline runs (applied-ml):
  - Run unit smoke tests: ensure model can load and run a 1-token and 512-token inference.
  - Run baseline prompt suite: generation, chat turn-taking, and embeddings tests.
  - Collect latency, memory, and token-cost metrics under standard synthetic load (see table below).
- Quality guardrails (applied-ml/product):
  - Run safety checklist: sensitive content detection, PII redaction tests.
  - Run hallucination/factuality tests: targeted fact-check prompt set.
  - Run style/format tests: structured output conformance.
- Quantization profiling (applied-ml/runtime):
  - Test recommended profiles (fp16, int8, q4_0/q4_1) on sample workloads.
  - Capture delta in accuracy metrics and latency improvement.
  - Identify fallback path for profiles with unacceptable degradation.
- Final gating and landing:
  - Generate onboarding report (template) and request reviewer sign-off.
  - Add model manifest to catalog including serving profiles and quantization recommendations.

5) Prompt sets & benchmark management
- Structure: each prompt set must include metadata fields: id, owner, date_created, intended_scenarios, input_schema, expected_output_schema, scoring_rules, and tags.
- Versioning: store prompt sets in git with semver-like tagging (v1.0.0). Changes that affect expected outputs require new version and re-eval of downstream models.
- Benchmarks: separate stable benchmark suites (regression benchmark) from exploratory suites (ad-hoc tests). Use an anchor model baseline for drift detection.
- Best practices:
  - Keep prompts small and reproducible; include seed and RNG settings in harness run.
  - Annotate prompts with acceptance criteria (pass/fail thresholds).
  - Include negative tests that assert unacceptable outputs are not produced.

6) Quality guardrails (definition and enforcement)
- Guardrail categories: safety, factuality, style/format, privacy, and performance.
- Enforcement levels: informational (monitoring), advisory (warnings), hard-gate (block onboarding if critical).
- Example checks and thresholds:
  - Safety: < 0.1% of responses flagged by safety detector for high-severity content across 1k prompt sample.
  - Factuality: BLEU/ROUGE-style or model-based fact-checker accuracy must be within 2% of anchor baseline for core factual prompts.
  - Response format: 100% conformance for structured-output tests.
  - Latency: p99 latency must meet the latency SLO for intended serving tier (see SLO table).

7) Quantization profiles and evaluation
- Profiles: canonical names and definitions: fp16 (baseline), int8 (fast path), q4_0, q4_1, q4_k.
- Test matrix: run each profile against the baseline using the following matrix: prompt types (short/long), batch sizes (1,4,16), and token lengths (32,256,1024).
- Metrics to capture: token-level accuracy (task-specific), end-to-end latency, memory usage, and rare-case failure rates.
- Decision rules: adopt a quantization profile if accuracy degradation <= 1.5% on critical prompts and latency improvement >= 20% or memory reduction >= 30%. If criteria not met, document tradeoffs and recommend hybrid routing.

8) Regression triage playbook (when detection occurs)
- Detection triggers:
  - New model rollout produces statistically significant drop on regression benchmark (p < 0.01) or automated quality alert triggers.
  - Production telemetry indicates higher error rates, safety hits, or SLO violations.
- Immediate actions (0-30 minutes):
  1. Create incident ticket and tag SMEs (applied-ml, runtime, SRE).
  2. If production impact is high, roll back to last-known-good model or route traffic to anchor model.
  3. Capture top 50 failing prompts and associated logs/artifacts.
- Analysis (30 minutes - 4 hours):
  1. Run targeted eval harness comparing new vs. anchor model on failing prompt set and full regression suite.
  2. Check for data drift, prompt drift, or config/regression in quantization.
  3. If quantization suspected, re-run baseline in fp16 to isolate.
- Remediation (4 hours - 5 days):
  - Fix options: prompt-tuning, model re-training, revert quantization, or update serving config (timeouts, batch sizes).
  - Post-fix: trigger full regression run before re-release.
- Communication: postmortem entry in confluence incident tracker and notify affected customers per escalation playbook.

9) Roles and ownership
- Model Owner: owns onboarding request, business acceptance criteria, and sign-off.
- Applied ML team: owns prompt set design, evaluation metrics, and triage.
- Serving/runtime team: owns quantization integration, perf profiling, and kerning selection tests.
- SRE/Observability: owns production monitors, alerting thresholds, and runbook execution.

10) Metrics, SLOs, and dashboards
- Recommended SLOs for eval harness runs:
  - Baseline throughput: ability to run standard regression suite in < 90 minutes on the CI cluster.
  - Coverage: >= 95% of regression benchmark executed per onboarding.
  - Freshness: prompt catalog updates must be tagged and published within 48 hours of change.
- Dashboards: per-model evaluation summary, prompt-level failure heatmap, quantization impact view, and regression trend timelines.

11) Example configuration table
| Field | Description | Example | Requirement |
| model_id | Unique model ID | redwood/gptx-13b | required |
| serving_tier | hosted | dedicated | required |
| quant_profiles | List of recommended profiles | [fp16,q4_1] | recommended |
| regression_suite | Benchmarks to run | core-factuality-v1 | required |
| owner | Human owner | @maya.patel | required |

12) CLI/runbook snippets
- Run a baseline regression:
  - ./eval-harness run --model redwood/gptx-13b --suite core-factuality-v1 --profile fp16 --out /artifacts/model-onboard-2026-05-01
- Quantization sweep (example):
  - ./quant-sweep --model ./weights --profiles q4_0,q4_1,int8 --batch-sizes 1,4,16 --out /artifacts/quant-sweep-2026-05-01

13) Release & rollout guidance
- Canary: start with 1% traffic to verify production metrics for 24 hours.
- Ramp: 1 -> 5 -> 25 -> 50 -> 100% with 24-hour observation windows.
- Fallback policy: instant rollback on critical safety hits or p99 latency breach > 2x SLO.

14) Appendix: templates and links
- Onboarding report template: link to Confluence onboarding template (internal).
- Prompt set schema (YAML example): link to prompt catalog README.
- Common failure modes: short list (tokenization mismatches, seed differences, quantization-induced hallucinations, prompt parsing errors).

Ownership and feedback
This document is maintained by Applied ML (Maya Patel). Send suggested edits or missing scenarios to the reviewer list. Major process changes require cross-team review (Applied ML, Runtime, SRE, Product).
